subStrands.Rw: Writers' use of language, structure and stylistic features
subStrands.Rv: Conventions, viewpoint, purpose, themes and ideas
subStrands.Wa: Content, register and language for genre, purpose and audience

7.text: Give an informed personal response to a text and provide some textual reference in support.
Understand how readers make choices about the texts they like reading, e.g. by author or genre.
Extract the main points and relevant information from a text or IT source, using a range of strategies such as skimming and scanning.
Select, collate and summarise ideas from texts, using notes where relevant.
Use inference and deduction to recognise implicit meanings.

7.subStrand: Writers' use of language, structure and stylistic features
7.text: Comment on a writer’s use of language, demonstrating an understanding of the implications of their use of vocabulary.

7.subStrand: Writers' use of language, structure and stylistic features
7.text: Identify and describe the effect of writers’ and poets’ use of literary, rhetorical and grammatical features, including imagery and figurative language.

7.subStrand: Writers' use of language, structure and stylistic features
7.text: Show awareness of poets’ use of language and its intended impact on the reader.

7.subStrand: Writers' use of language, structure and stylistic features
7.text: Use the terms ‘image’, ‘simile’, ‘metaphor’, ‘onomatopoeia’, ‘setting’ and ‘genre’ in discussion about texts.

7.subStrand: Writers' use of language, structure and stylistic features
7.text: Comment on the use of formal and informal language and discuss the writer’s motivation for making the choice.

7.subStrand: Writers' use of language, structure and stylistic features
7.text: Show awareness of the reasons for using long and short sentences.

7.subStrand: Writers' use of language, structure and stylistic features
7.text: Comment on how the choice of sentences and variety of sentence openings control pace and meaning.

7.subStrand: Writers' use of language, structure and stylistic features
7.text: Explore the variety and range of ways in which the content of texts can be organised, structured and combined.

7.subStrand: Conventions, viewpoint, purpose, themes and ideas
7.text: Identify and understand the main ideas, viewpoints, themes and purposes in a text. Support comments by quotation from more than one location in the text.

7.subStrand: Conventions, viewpoint, purpose, themes and ideas
7.text: Demonstrate understanding of features of narrative and non-narrative texts by explaining and developing these features in their own discussion and writing.

7.subStrand: Conventions, viewpoint, purpose, themes and ideas
7.text: Understand the different ways texts can reflect the social, cultural and historical contexts in which they were written.

7.subStrand: Conventions, viewpoint, purpose, themes and ideas
7.text: Explore the range of different ways writers use layout, form and presentation in a variety of texts.
Practise note-taking using different styles for different purposes.
Use a dictionary and thesaurus effectively to further develop vocabulary.

7.subStrand: Content, register and language for genre, purpose and audience
7.text: Use a range of planning formats or methods to develop different ways of generating, organising and shaping ideas.

7.subStrand: Content, register and language for genre, purpose and audience
7.text: Create an effect by using some of the key linguistic and literary techniques used by writers.

7.subStrand: Content, register and language for genre, purpose and audience
7.text: Begin to develop character and voice in fiction writing.

7.subStrand: Content, register and language for genre, purpose and audience
7.text: Use features and conventions of a wide variety of text types in order to write to inform, explain, describe, argue, persuade and comment.

7.subStrand: Content, register and language for genre, purpose and audience
7.text: Understand and use degrees of formality in a range of texts according to context, purpose and audience.

7.subStrand: Content, register and language for genre, purpose and audience
7.text: Write to express a personal viewpoint.

7.subStrand: Content, register and language for genre, purpose and audience
7.text: Learn a range of vocabulary appropriate to their needs, and use words precisely in speech and writing to clarify and extend meaning and to interest their audience.

7.subStrand: Content, register and language for genre, purpose and audience
7.text: Clarify and extend meaning and create specific effects by using a range of features, e.g. precise and imaginative use of vocabulary.

7.subStrand: Content, register and language for genre, purpose and audience
7.text: Understand the conventions of standard English and how to use them consistently in writing.
Shape the overall organisation, sequence and presentation of a text to convey ideas clearly and effectively.
Mirror the purpose of the writing by appropriate use of paragraphs and selection of linking words and phrases.
Provide clarity and emphasis in writing, using a variety of sentence lengths, structures and subjects.
Provide appropriate detail and clarify relationships between setting, characters, themes, plot, etc. by using a range of features, e.g. varying sentence length and structure.
Use a range of increasingly complex sentence structures to communicate meaning and to give fluency to their writing.
Build up detail and convey shades of meaning through sentence structure, e.g. controlling order of clauses, expanding verb phrases.
Use correct grammar, including articles, word order and tense in a range of genres and text types.
Clarify relationships between ideas with an accurate and increased use of connectives.
Use a wide range of punctuation to make meaning clear, including generally accurate use of commas in complex sentences and dialogue.
Spell correctly most commonly used words with regular patterns.
Increase knowledge of word families, roots, derivations, morphology and regular spelling patterns.
Speak for a variety of purposes, such as to explain, describe, narrate, explore, analyse, imagine, discuss, argue and persuade.
Deliberately shape talk for clarity and effect and to engage listener.
Use a range of vocabulary appropriate to context, and use language to clarify meaning and to interest and convince their audience.
Practise speaking fluently and clearly at an appropriate pace and volume.
Develop the ability to listen courteously to others and be sensitive to turn taking.
Begin to make significant contributions to group discussions, engaging with complex material, making perceptive responses and showing awareness of a speaker’s aims.
Work in solo, paired and group assignments, including role-play.
Through role-play, show insight into texts and issues through choice of speech, gesture and movement.
Explain features of own and others’ language, showing sensitivity to the impact of varying language for different purposes and situations.
